slides.title: Claude joins the call
body: Anthropic **launched Claude Meetings this week**. Teams can add Claude to a video call as a visible participant. It follows the conversation and starts working on tasks while people are still talking.

slides.title: It drafts as you talk
body: As the team talks, Claude can **draft the plan**, map a timeline on a whiteboard and answer in the meeting chat. It can also pull figures, such as last year's event spending, from connected work apps.

slides.title: Notes land in Claude
body: Afterward, the notes, action items and materials Claude made are available in claude.ai. Claude saves a transcript, a summary and descriptions of what was on screen. **Audio is not saved.**

slides.title: Beta, Meet only, no guests
body: It is a **beta** on Claude's business plans, and works with **Google Meet** only for now. By default Claude stays out of calls with outside guests and leaves if one joins, unless an admin allows it.

slides.title: Free for now, partly
body: Notes, transcripts and most in-call answers are free during the beta. Documents and whiteboards have a **free-use deadline of Feb 10, 2027**. Per VentureBeat, Team seats list at **$20** per user per month on annual billing, or $25 monthly.

sources.title: Anthropic launches Claude Meetings to turn workplace discussions into plans and tasks
Anthropic brings Claude into Google Meet to draft documents and whiteboards during your meetings

facts.text: Anthropic announced Claude Meetings on Tuesday (Nov 10, 2026), which brings Claude into video calls to begin working on tasks while participants are still talking.

Teams can add Claude to a video call as a visible participant; as participants talk, it can draft the plan being discussed, map out a timeline on a whiteboard, answer questions in the meeting chat, and access connected work apps to retrieve information such as last year's figures.
After the call, the meeting notes, action items and other materials Claude created are available in claude.ai.

Claude identifies itself as a meeting participant and posts a notice in the meeting chat. It won't join calls with external guests unless authorized by an admin, and will automatically leave if an external guest joins.
Claude Meetings is launching in beta on Team and Enterprise plans. At launch it works with Google Meet.
Anthropic says Claude saves the transcript, a summary, and descriptions of what appeared on screen. Audio is excluded from that record.

Notes, transcripts and most in-call answers are included at no extra charge during the beta. Documents, whiteboards and other materials Claude creates in a meeting have a separate free-use deadline of February 10, 2027.
Anthropic's pricing page lists Team standard seats at $20 per user per month with annual billing or $25 with monthly billing.
By default, Claude stays out when the invite includes someone from outside the organization and leaves if an outside guest joins midway; admins can allow Claude on those calls.

caption:
Anthropic launched Claude Meetings this week: Claude can join a Google Meet call and draft the plan while people talk.

It is a beta on Claude's business plans, and it has limits.

→ Claude joins as a visible participant, drafts plans, maps timelines on a whiteboard and pulls figures from connected work apps
→ It saves a transcript, summary and on-screen descriptions, not audio, and by default stays out of calls with outside guests
→ Notes and most in-call answers are free in the beta; documents and whiteboards are free to use until Feb 10, 2027

Would you want an AI in your next meeting?

Source: TechCrunch, "Anthropic launches Claude Meetings to turn workplace discussions into plans and tasks", Nov 10, 2026; VentureBeat, "Anthropic brings Claude into Google Meet to draft documents and whiteboards during your meetings", Nov 12, 2026.
